Iteration 1/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: Initial hypotheses prioritize established dependency logic in lung adenocarcinoma-like cells and binary molecular predictors with adequate cell counts. Negative direction means the exposed group is expected to show stronger dependency (more negative CRISPR score); positive direction means weaker dependency (less negative score). Expected effects include oncogene addiction for KRAS, BRAF V600E, EGFR amplification, and ERBB2 amplification; pathway crosstalk effects such as reduced BRAF dependency in KRAS mutants and increased STAT3 dependency with EGFR amplification; KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 dependency; TP53-loss/MDM2 synthetic relationship; MSI-high/WRN synthetic lethality; SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 synthetic lethality; and MYC-amplification effects on transcriptional and USP7 dependencies. Analyses are restricted to CRISPR-QC cells and DNA-omics-measured samples to avoid imputed molecular states. All are marked unresolved pending discovery evidence and uncertainty.

record.narrative: Discovery evidence strongly supports two mechanistic synthetic-lethal associations: MSI-high cells show much stronger WRN dependency and SMARCA4-loss cells show much stronger SMARCA2 dependency. These signed estimates are positive for their negative-direction hypotheses, indicating more negative dependency scores in the exposed groups, and their magnitudes are many multiples of the approximate 10% relative scale based on absolute outcome means. These are accepted as dataset-specific associations; causality and generalizability are not implied. The EGFR amplification-EGFR dependency association is plausible and point size exceeds the 10% threshold, but its lower bound is very close to zero and this was among 12 initial tests, so I keep it unresolved pending independent validation. Most direct oncogene and transcriptional dependencies are small or uncertain. For H2, H3, and H5, the 95% intervals exclude clinically meaningful effects in the registered direction; these are rejected as not supporting the original clinically meaningful associations. H7 is the opposite: KEAP1 loss is strongly associated with a direction opposite to the registered hypothesis, so the original claim is rejected and a reversed claim is proposed for later testing. Several remaining molecular associations remain unresolved because intervals include zero and clinically relevant values.

record.narrative:
Independent validation for the EGFR-amplification association with dependency_EGFR (H4) does not support accepting the claim. Discovery R4, signed to the negative-dependency hypothesis, was positive and slightly larger than the approximate 10% relative-difference threshold, but its 95% interval remained very close to zero. Independent validation R13 is signed negative, with a wide interval including zero and both clinically meaningful positive and negative ranges. The two evidence sources are inconsistent, and the validated data do not provide a stable clinically meaningful association; I therefore keep H4 unresolved but close the direct investigation rather than accept it. This does not prove absence; a subgroup effect could remain hidden, so I registered an interaction test between EGFR amplification and KRAS wild-type status.

I also reassessed the reversed KEAP1-loss claim H13. The parent discovery R7 was enormous relative to the NFE2L2 outcome scale: KEAP1-loss cells showed substantially less negative dependency_NFE2L2 than non-loss cells, with the 95% interval entirely on the side of clinically meaningful effect. This strongly supports the reversed dataset-specific association H13, even though the original mechanistic direction H7 was rejected. I accepted H13 and closed its direct investigation.

I reassessed MYC-amplification versus POLR2A dependency H9. Its signed estimate is tiny and the upper confidence limit is below the approximate 10% relative threshold, so I rejected it as not supporting a clinically meaningful difference.

Current supported dataset-specific findings are: MSI-high cells have much stronger WRN dependency; SMARCA4-loss cells have much stronger SMARCA2 dependency; and KEAP1-loss cells have much weaker NFE2L2 dependency. Current negative findings include rejected KRAS-mutation effects on BRAF dependency, BRAF V600E on BRAF dependency, EGFR amplification on STAT3 dependency, TP53-loss effect on MDM2 dependency in the original direction, and MYC amplification effect on POLR2A dependency. Current unresolved uncertainty includes KRAS mutation on KRAS dependency, ERBB2 amplification on ERBB2 dependency, TP53 loss on MDM2 dependency, MYC amplification on USP7 dependency, and EGFR amplification on EGFR dependency. The next analyses focus on heterogeneity of the three strong effects across lineage subtype and constructed research markers, plus one mechanistic EGFR/KRAS subgroup interaction.

Iteration 2/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: Registered new comparisons that refine the three dataset-specific synthetic-lethal/cancer-dependency signals, test their robustness across lineage, library, and culture context, and add mechanistically related broad-exploration tests. For KRAS dependency, the original all-sample association was small and unresolved; a lung adenocarcinoma-only test is a scientifically meaningful refinement. For MSI-high/WRN, SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2, and KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2, I registered direct subgroup mean differences within adenocarcinoma to obtain interpretable within-subgroup effect sizes, and interaction tests by lineage subtype, Ky library, and adherent culture to assess whether these large effects are stable or context-specific. The new ARID1A-loss versus SMARCA2 dependency comparison probes another SWI/SNF complex context, and the KEAP1-loss versus USP7 dependency comparison tests pathway crosstalk around NFE2L2 regulation. All comparisons use CRISPR-QC and DNA-omics-measured cells and are marked unresolved before analysis.

prompt:
Iteration 2/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

record.narrative: Selecting twelve registered analyses to refine and stress-test the strongest accepted dataset-specific associations while also following up two unresolved mechanistic leads. First, run within-adenocarcinoma mean differences for WRN/MSI-high, SMARCA2/SMARCA4-loss, and NFE2L2/KEAP1-loss because adenocarcinoma is the dominant lineage and within-subgroup effect estimates are clinically interpretable. Second, run lineage-subtype interaction tests for the same three associations to determine whether these large effects differ between adenocarcinoma and non-adenocarcinoma cells. Third, run CRISPR-library ky interaction tests to assess whether the accepted synthetic-lethal or loss-of-function dependencies remain robust across screen library context. Fourth, run the EGFR-amplification by KRAS-wild-type interaction to investigate whether the inconsistent direct EGFR dependency signal is restricted to a mechanistic subgroup. Finally, run two new mechanistically related comparisons: ARID1A-loss with SMARCA2 dependency, because ARID1A is another SWI/SNF subunit, and KEAP1-loss with USP7 dependency, because it probes pathway crosstalk around the very large KEAP1/NFE2L2 signal. These tests maximize information from the newly registered claims without rerunning already estimated primary associations.

record.narrative:
The new adenocarcinoma-restricted direct tests strongly confirm the three already accepted dataset-specific dependency associations. For MSI-high versus WRN in adenocarcinoma, the signed estimate is +0.784 with a narrow 95% interval [0.748, 0.821], far exceeding an approximate 10% threshold based on the WRN score scale; I accept H25 as a dataset-specific subgroup association. For SMARCA4-loss versus SMARCA2 in adenocarcinoma, the signed estimate is +0.775 [0.752, 0.798], again a very large and precise association; I accept H26. For KEAP1-loss versus weaker NFE2L2 dependency in adenocarcinoma, the signed estimate is +0.795 [0.769, 0.820], accepting H27 as the same reversed KEAP1/NFE2L2 relationship seen in the full eligible sample.

The lineage-subtype interaction tests mostly do not show strong evidence that the main effects differ between adenocarcinoma and non-adenocarcinoma cells. H15 rejects an SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 subtype interaction because the signed interval excludes clinically meaningful support in the claimed direction. H14 and H16 have signed point estimates near zero or opposite to the claimed direction, but their intervals include clinically meaningful values in the claimed direction, so I keep them unresolved but deferred rather than claiming precise absence. These are same-dataset subgroup contrasts, not independent validation, and they involve multiplicity and uneven cell sizes.

Library ky context tests are informative. H28 shows no clinically meaningful ky interaction for MSI-high/WRN because the signed interval excludes meaningful support in the claimed direction; reject and close. H30 for KEAP1/NFE2L2 is near zero and opposite to the claimed direction, though imprecise, so I leave it unresolved but deferred. H29 is the one notable borderline finding: the signed SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 ky interaction is +0.044 [ -0.003, 0.091], just around the approximate 10% SMARCA2 scale threshold. The interval crosses zero and includes both negligible and meaningful values, so it cannot support a stable library-context modification; I keep H29 active and propose a direct ky-subgroup SMARCA2 test to clarify it. I also propose direct ky tests for WRN and NFE2L2 to interpret the small imprecise ky interaction estimates.

The EGFR-amplification interaction within KRAS wild-type cells, H20, does not support the failed direct EGFR dependency signal: the signed estimate is small and opposite, though the interval is wide enough to include a clinically meaningful effect in the claimed direction. Given the earlier inconsistent validation for H4, I defer further EGFR subgroup work. ARID1A-loss versus SMARCA2 dependency is negligible, H34, and KEAP1-loss versus USP7 dependency, H35, is small and imprecise; both remain unresolved only because intervals include some clinically meaningful values, but they are low priority. I request independent validation for H11 because MSI-high/WRN is a large, mechanistically meaningful synthetic-lethal signal with relatively small MSI-high exposure count in discovery, and external validation would strengthen the accepted association. All conclusions remain dataset-specific associations, not causal claims or guaranteed generalizable findings.

prompt:
Iteration 2/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

For MSI-high/WRN, SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2, and KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2, I registered direct subgroup mean differences within adenocarcinoma to obtain interpretable within-subgroup effect sizes, and interaction tests by lineage subtype, Ky library, and adherent culture to assess whether these large effects are stable or context-specific. All comparisons use CRISPR-QC and DNA-omics-measured cells and are marked unresolved before analysis.","analyze":"Selecting twelve registered analyses to refine and stress-test the strongest accepted dataset-specific associations while also following up two unresolved mechanistic leads. Second, run lineage-subtype interaction tests for the same three associations to determine whether these large effects differ between adenocarcinoma and non-adenocarcinoma cells. Third, run CRISPR-library ky interaction tests to assess whether the accepted synthetic-lethal or loss-of-function dependencies remain robust across screen library context. Fourth, run the EGFR-amplification by KRAS-wild-type interaction to investigate whether the inconsistent direct EGFR dependency signal is restricted to a mechanistic subgroup. Finally, run two new mechanistically related comparisons: ARID1A-loss with SMARCA2 dependency, because ARID1A is another SWI/SNF subunit, and KEAP1-loss with USP7 dependency, because it probes pathway crosstalk around the very large KEAP1/NFE2L2 signal. These tests maximize information from the newly registered claims without rerunning already estimated primary associations.","appraise":"The new adenocarcinoma-restricted direct tests strongly confirm the three already accepted dataset-specific dependency associations. For SMARCA4-loss versus SMARCA2 in adenocarcinoma, the signed estimate is +0.775 [0.752, 0.798], again a very large and precise association; I accept H26. For KEAP1-loss versus weaker NFE2L2 dependency in adenocarcinoma, the signed estimate is +0.795 [0.769, 0.820], accepting H27 as the same reversed KEAP1/NFE2L2 relationship seen in the full eligible sample.\n\nThe lineage-subtype interaction tests mostly do not show strong evidence that the main effects differ between adenocarcinoma and non-adenocarcinoma cells. H15 rejects an SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 subtype interaction because the signed interval excludes clinically meaningful support in the claimed direction. H14 and H16 have signed point estimates near zero or opposite to the claimed direction, but their intervals include clinically meaningful values in the claimed direction, so I keep them unresolved but deferred rather than claiming precise absence. These are same-dataset subgroup contrasts, not independent validation, and they involve multiplicity and uneven cell sizes.\n\nLibrary ky context tests are informative. record.narrative:
The newly delivered independent validation for H11 strongly supports the MSI-high association with stronger WRN dependency. Discovery R11, signed to the negative-dependency hypothesis, was +0.790 with a 95% interval [0.760, 0.820]. Independent validation R26 was +0.797 with an independent interval [0.744, 0.850] under stricter validation-adjusted coverage. Both lower bounds are far above any approximate 10% clinically relevant threshold on the WRN dependency score scale, and the two estimates are highly consistent. I therefore accept H11 as a robust dataset-specific association and close its direct investigation because the central direct claim has now been internally validated. This does not establish causality in cells or generalizable clinical utility; it establishes that the supplied data and supplied independent validation both show a large MSI-high versus WRN dependency-score difference.

With H11 replicated, the strongest evidence in the project remains the trio of large dependency-score associations: MSI-high cells show stronger WRN dependency (H11, replicated; H25 adenocarcinoma-restricted), SMARCA4-loss cells show stronger SMARCA2 dependency (H12; H26 adenocarcinoma-restricted), and KEAP1-loss cells show weaker NFE2L2 dependency (H13; H27 adenocarcinoma-restricted). The first of these is now the most secure claim in the accepted set. The current context results are mostly reassuring but incomplete. Lineage-subtype interaction tests suggest no strong evidence of SMARCA4-loss effect modification by subtype (H15 rejected), while WRN and NFE2L2 subtype interactions remain imprecise but low priority. Library ky context tests showed no meaningful WRN interaction (H28 rejected) and an imprecise near-null NFE2L2 interaction (H30 deferred); the SMARCA2 ky interaction is borderline and unresolved (H29), so the newly registered direct ky subgroup test H36 is important. Adherent-culture interactions are pending, and I registered direct adherent-subgroup mean differences for WRN/MSI-high, SMARCA2/SMARCA4-loss, and NFE2L2/KEAP1-loss because these will provide interpretable within-culture effect sizes rather than only interaction contrasts.

Negative findings remain important: KRAS mutation on BRAF dependency, BRAF V600E on BRAF dependency, EGFR amplification on STAT3 dependency, the original KEAP1-loss stronger-NFE2L2 hypothesis, MYC amplification on POLR2A dependency, the SMARCA4-loss by subtype interaction, and the MSI-high by ky library interaction for WRN were rejected as not supporting clinically meaningful effects in their registered directions. Unresolved uncertainty remains for direct KRAS/EGFR/ERBB2/TP53/MYC associations, the EGFR/KRAS-wild-type subgroup interaction, low-priority library and subtype interactions, ARID1A-loss on SMARCA2, KEAP1-loss on USP7, and the pending context analyses. The most informative next analyses are the direct ky tests H36-H38, the new direct adherent tests, and then the marker/context tests. If the context tests remain broadly consistent, the next independent validation should prioritize H12, because it is a large mechanistically meaningful association without independent replication; H13 would be the next candidate. If a context test shows strong attenuation or heterogeneity, that should be investigated before spending additional validation on that pathway.

independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

expectation

and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep

parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Maintain multiplicity caution and no causal/generalizability claims without validation.","latest_stage_narratives":{"explore":"Registered new comparisons that refine the three dataset-specific synthetic-lethal/cancer-dependency signals, test their robustness across lineage, library, and culture context, and add mechanistically related broad-exploration tests. For MSI-high/WRN, SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2, and KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2, I registered direct subgroup mean differences within adenocarcinoma to obtain interpretable within-subgroup effect sizes, and interaction tests by lineage subtype, Ky library, and adherent culture to assess whether these large effects are stable or context-specific. The new ARID1A-loss versus SMARCA2 dependency comparison probes another SWI/SNF complex context, and the KEAP1-loss versus USP7 dependency comparison tests pathway crosstalk around NFE2L2 regulation. All comparisons use CRISPR-QC and DNA-omics-measured cells and are marked unresolved before analysis.","analyze":"Selecting twelve registered analyses to refine and stress-test the strongest accepted dataset-specific associations while also following up two unresolved mechanistic leads. First, run within-adenocarcinoma mean differences for WRN/MSI-high, SMARCA2/SMARCA4-loss, and NFE2L2/KEAP1-loss because adenocarcinoma is the dominant lineage and within-subgroup effect estimates are clinically interpretable. Second, run lineage-subtype interaction tests for the same three associations to determine whether these large effects differ between adenocarcinoma and non-adenocarcinoma cells. Third, run CRISPR-library ky interaction tests to assess whether the accepted synthetic-lethal or loss-of-function dependencies remain robust across screen library context. Fourth, run the EGFR-amplification by KRAS-wild-type interaction to investigate whether the inconsistent direct EGFR dependency signal is restricted to a mechanistic subgroup. Finally, run two new mechanistically related comparisons: ARID1A-loss with SMARCA2 dependency, because ARID1A is another SWI/SNF subunit, and KEAP1-loss with USP7 dependency, because it probes pathway crosstalk around the very large KEAP1/NFE2L2 signal. These tests maximize information from the newly registered claims without rerunning already estimated primary associations.","appraise":"The new adenocarcinoma-restricted direct tests strongly confirm the three already accepted dataset-specific dependency associations. For MSI-high versus WRN in adenocarcinoma, the signed estimate is +0.784 with a narrow 95% interval [0.748, 0.821], far exceeding an approximate 10% threshold based on the WRN score scale; I accept H25 as a dataset-specific subgroup association. For SMARCA4-loss versus SMARCA2 in adenocarcinoma, the signed estimate is +0.775 [0.752, 0.798], again a very large and precise association; I accept H26. For KEAP1-loss versus weaker NFE2L2 dependency in adenocarcinoma, the signed estimate is +0.795 [0.769, 0.820], accepting H27 as the same reversed KEAP1/NFE2L2 relationship seen in the full eligible sample.\n\nThe lineage-subtype interaction tests mostly do not show strong evidence that the main effects differ between adenocarcinoma and non-adenocarcinoma cells. H15 rejects an SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 subtype interaction because the signed interval excludes clinically meaningful support in the claimed direction. H14 and H16 have signed point estimates near zero or opposite to the claimed direction, but their intervals include clinically meaningful values in the claimed direction, so I keep them unresolved but deferred rather than claiming precise absence. These are same-dataset subgroup contrasts, not independent validation, and they involve multiplicity and uneven cell sizes.\n\nLibrary ky context tests are informative. H28 shows no clinically meaningful ky interaction for MSI-high/WRN because the signed interval excludes meaningful support in the claimed direction; reject and close. H30 for KEAP1/NFE2L2 is near zero and opposite to the claimed direction, though imprecise, so I leave it unresolved but deferred. H29 is the one notable borderline finding: the signed SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 ky interaction is +0.044 [ -0.003, 0.091], just around the approximate 10% SMARCA2 scale threshold. The interval crosses zero and includes both negligible and meaningful values, so it cannot support a stable library-context modification; I keep H29 active and propose a direct ky-subgroup SMARCA2 test to clarify it. I also propose direct ky tests for WRN and NFE2L2 to interpret the small imprecise ky interaction estimates.\n\nThe EGFR-amplification interaction within KRAS wild-type cells, H20, does not support the failed direct EGFR dependency signal: the signed estimate is small and opposite, though the interval is wide enough to include a clinically meaningful effect in the claimed direction. Both lower bounds are far above any approximate 10% clinically relevant threshold on the WRN dependency score scale, and the two estimates are highly consistent. I therefore accept H11 as a robust dataset-specific association and close its direct investigation because the central direct claim has now been internally validated. record.narrative: Registered new mechanistically motivated comparisons targeting outcome–predictor pairs not yet explored, while retaining the accepted WRN/MSI-high, SMARCA2/SMARCA4-loss, and NFE2L2/KEAP1-loss findings for follow-up context checks. The new RIT1 panel tests upstream RTK-to-RAS/MAPK signaling logic: KRAS and BRAF mutant cells are hypothesized to be less dependent on upstream RIT1, so their dependency scores should be less negative than in wild-type cells (positive raw difference), whereas ERBB2 or EGFR amplification could reflect receptor-driven signaling that still uses RIT1 and thus could be associated with stronger RIT1 dependency (more negative scores). The EGFR/RIT1 direction is deliberately uncertain because the direct EGFR/dependency_EGFR claim was not externally consistent, but testing RIT1 asks a distinct mechanistic question. MYC amplification versus dependency_DHX9 tests whether transcription-factor amplification creates a helicase/transcription-stress dependency beyond the null MYC/POLR2A result. TP53 loss versus dependency_RPL11 and dependency_USP7 extends p53-pathway dependency logic: TP53 loss should reduce reliance on p53-pathway nodes, giving less negative scores. The MDM2 interaction refinement asks whether the weak TP53-loss effect is modified by MTAP loss, a co-deleted p53-region alteration that could alter MDM2-pathway context. Finally, EGFR amplification versus TMED10 probes whether RTK-amplified cells are more dependent on secretory-pathway cargo trafficking. These proposals improve broad coverage of the untested dependency scores and provide falsifiable alternatives to the current accepted synthetic-lethal associations. The next analysis phase should prioritize these new tests together with the highest-value pending context tests: direct ky-library SMARCA2 dependency and direct adherent-culture tests for the accepted associations. Marker D/E/F tests and lower-priority KRAS subtype/culture interactions can be deferred unless they become mechanistically or robustness-priority based on results. All claims remain dataset-specific associations; validation will be used to distinguish replication from incidental dataset structure.

Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

record.narrative: Selected twelve existing analyses that split between robustness follow-up of the accepted dependency associations and new mechanistic broad-exploration tests. First, I prioritize direct within-context mean differences for the three large accepted associations in Ky library and adherent culture contexts: H36 for SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 in Ky, H37 for MSI-high/WRN in Ky, H38 for KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 in Ky, and H39-H41 for the same predictors in adherent culture. These are more interpretable than interaction contrasts and are needed because the Ky interaction for SMARCA2/H29 was borderline while the WRN and NFE2L2 Ky interactions were imprecise but not supportive. Direct adherent tests assess whether the accepted effects persist in the dominant culture context rather than only in the full eligible sample. Second, I run six untested mechanistic comparisons: H42-H44 test RTK-to-RAS/MAPK signaling logic around RIT1 dependency under KRAS mutation, BRAF V600E, and ERBB2 amplification; H46 tests whether MYC amplification is associated with stronger DHX9 dependency, a plausible transcription-stress/helicase relationship distinct from the null MYC/POLR2A result; and H47-H48 test whether TP53 loss is associated with weaker dependency on p53-pathway components RPL11 and USP7. I do not run arbitrary research-marker tests or the MDM2/MTAP interaction because their prior mechanistic specificity is lower and existing unresolved claims are already low priority. I also defer EGFR/RIT1 and TMED10 tests because the EGFR-dependency signals have been inconsistent and these hypotheses are more speculative.

evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative:
The new direct context tests strongly support the three previously accepted dependency associations. For SMARCA4-loss versus dependency_SMARCA2 within the Ky library, R27 is signed to the negative-dependency hypothesis and is +0.814 with a 95% interval [0.774, 0.855]. This is far above a conservative ~10% score-scale benchmark and resolves the earlier borderline Ky interaction by showing that the main SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 effect remains very large inside Ky cells. For MSI-high versus dependency_WRN within Ky, R28 is +0.751 [0.693, 0.809]; although the exposed Ky/MSI-high cell has only 27 observations, the lower bound remains enormous, so I accept it as a dataset-specific context association while noting small-cell caution. For KEAP1-loss versus weaker NFE2L2 dependency within Ky, R29 is +0.787 [0.741, 0.832]. The adherent-culture direct tests are similarly strong: WRN/MSI-high +0.816 [0.784, 0.849], SMARCA2/SMARCA4-loss +0.786 [0.762, 0.810], and NFE2L2/KEAP1-loss +0.795 [0.770, 0.820]. I accept H36-H41 as dataset-specific within-context associations supporting the robustness of the accepted trio, not as independent validation.

The most important new mechanistic result is TP53 loss versus dependency_USP7. With direction +1, a positive signed estimate means TP53-loss cells have less negative USP7 dependency scores, i.e., weaker USP7 dependency. R38 is +0.804 [0.783, 0.825], an extremely large and precise dataset-specific association. It is mechanistically plausible because USP7 functions in p53/MDM2-related regulation, and TP53 loss could reduce reliance on USP7; however, this remains only an association in the supplied data. I accept H48 and keep it active, with context follow-up proposed before deciding whether it should become a leading validated claim.

The other new mechanistic tests are mostly null or imprecise. KRAS mutation versus dependency_RIT1, R33, is +0.003 with interval [-0.016, 0.023]; the upper bound is below the approximate 10% RIT1 score-scale benchmark, so I reject H42. BRAF V600E versus RIT1, R34, and ERBB2 amplification versus RIT1, R35, are near zero but have wide intervals that touch borderline clinically meaningful values in their claimed directions; H43 and H44 remain unresolved but deferred because the point estimates are negligible and the RIT1 panel otherwise gives little support. MYC amplification versus DHX9, R36, is near null with a borderline negative lower bound, so H46 is unresolved but deferred. TP53 loss versus RPL11, R37, is also near null with a borderline positive upper bound, so H47 is unresolved but deferred.

I request independent validation for H12. The central SMARCA4-loss/dependency_SMARCA2 association is large in the full eligible sample and now shows very large direct effects in adenocarcinoma, Ky, and adherent contexts; external validation would distinguish robust replication from shared same-dataset structure or correlated genomic confounding. H48 is the next validation candidate after its context tests, and H13 would remain a later candidate. All conclusions remain associations in this dataset; unadjusted Welch comparisons can be confounded by correlated alterations, multiple testing is present, and no causal or broadly generalizable claim is made.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).

If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;

status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.

record.narrative:
The new validation decisively strengthens H12 and disposes of the unresolved H4. For H12, SMARCA4-loss versus dependency_SMARCA2, discovery R12 was +0.782 [0.761, 0.802], signed to the hypothesis that SMARCA4-loss cells have stronger, more negative SMARCA2 dependency. Independent validation R39 was +0.805 [0.775, 0.836] under the stricter validation-adjusted interval. The lower bounds are far above any reasonable approximate 10% effect benchmark on the SMARCA2 score scale, and discovery and validation magnitudes are highly consistent. Therefore H12 is accepted as an independently replicated dataset-specific association, not as a causal or clinical claim. The previously accepted within-context confirmations H26 adenocarcinoma, H36 Ky library, and H40 adherent culture are now treated as completed robustness checks and closed. record.narrative: The next highest-value exploration is to resolve whether the very large TP53-loss/weaker-USP7 association is robust and whether it is confounded or modified by MTAP loss, a common co-deleted 9p alteration near CDKN2A/p53-related biology. I therefore registered a direct USP7 context test within MTAP-loss cells, a direct MTAP-loss effect on USP7, and a direct MTAP-loss effect on MDM2. If the USP7 association is stable across TP53-loss contexts and is not merely tracking MTAP co-loss, H48 should become the next independent validation target. I also registered downstream RAS/MAPK cross-dependency tests: KRAS or BRAF alterations may reduce dependence on upstream EGFR or KRAS itself, and KRAS mutation may reduce dependence on ERBB2. These are distinct from the earlier rejected EGFR-amplification results and test pathway position rather than receptor amplification. ERBB2 amplification versus STAT3 and TMED10 tests receptor-driven signaling dependencies beyond EGFR amplification. Finally, I registered TP53-loss versus POLR2A and DHX9 to ask whether p53 loss changes transcription-stress or helicase/R-loop dependencies, and a SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 context test within ARID1A-loss cells because ARID1A loss may modify chromatin-remodeler dependencies even though the direct ARID1A effect was null. These proposals preserve the current validation plan: first confirm H48 contexts, then request independent validation for H48 if consistent; H13 remains the next major unvalidated candidate after that.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.

and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.

Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

expectation
