Maintain caution: unadjusted Welch comparisons may reflect correlated genomic alterations, multiple testing, and dataset-specific structure; accepted claims are associations, not causal or generalizable clinical findings.","latest_stage_narratives":{"explore":"The next highest-value exploration is to resolve whether the very large TP53-loss/weaker-USP7 association is robust and whether it is confounded or modified by MTAP loss, a common co-deleted 9p alteration near CDKN2A/p53-related biology. I therefore registered a direct USP7 context test within MTAP-loss cells, a direct MTAP-loss effect on USP7, and a direct MTAP-loss effect on MDM2. If the USP7 association is stable across TP53-loss contexts and is not merely tracking MTAP co-loss, H48 should become the next independent validation target. I also registered downstream RAS/MAPK cross-dependency tests: KRAS or BRAF alterations may reduce dependence on upstream EGFR or KRAS itself, and KRAS mutation may reduce dependence on ERBB2. These are distinct from the earlier rejected EGFR-amplification results and test pathway position rather than receptor amplification. ERBB2 amplification versus STAT3 and TMED10 tests receptor-driven signaling dependencies beyond EGFR amplification. Finally, I registered TP53-loss versus POLR2A and DHX9 to ask whether p53 loss changes transcription-stress or helicase/R-loop dependencies, and a SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 context test within ARID1A-loss cells because ARID1A loss may modify chromatin-remodeler dependencies even though the direct ARID1A effect was null. These proposals preserve the current validation plan: first confirm H48 contexts, then request independent validation for H48 if consistent; H13 remains the next major unvalidated candidate after that.","analyze":"Selected twelve existing analyses that split between robustness follow-up of the accepted dependency associations and new mechanistic broad-exploration tests. First, I prioritize direct within-context mean differences for the three large accepted associations in Ky library and adherent culture contexts: H36 for SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 in Ky, H37 for MSI-high/WRN in Ky, H38 for KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 in Ky, and H39-H41 for the same predictors in adherent culture. These are more interpretable than interaction contrasts and are needed because the Ky interaction for SMARCA2/H29 was borderline while the WRN and NFE2L2 Ky interactions were imprecise but not supportive. Direct adherent tests assess whether the accepted effects persist in the dominant culture context rather than only in the full eligible sample. Second, I run six untested mechanistic comparisons: H42-H44 test RTK-to-RAS/MAPK signaling logic around RIT1 dependency under KRAS mutation, BRAF V600E, and ERBB2 amplification; H46 tests whether MYC amplification is associated with stronger DHX9 dependency, a plausible transcription-stress/helicase relationship distinct from the null MYC/POLR2A result; and H47-H48 test whether TP53 loss is associated with weaker dependency on p53-pathway components RPL11 and USP7. I do not run arbitrary research-marker tests or the MDM2/MTAP interaction because their prior mechanistic specificity is lower and existing unresolved claims are already low priority. I also defer EGFR/RIT1 and TMED10 tests because the EGFR-dependency signals have been inconsistent and these hypotheses are more speculative.","appraise":"The new direct context tests strongly support the three previously accepted dependency associations. For SMARCA4-loss versus dependency_SMARCA2 within the Ky library, R27 is signed to the negative-dependency hypothesis and is +0.814 with a 95% interval [0.774, 0.855]. This is far above a conservative ~10% score-scale benchmark and resolves the earlier borderline Ky interaction by showing that the main SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 effect remains very large inside Ky cells. For MSI-high versus dependency_WRN within Ky, R28 is +0.751 [0.693, 0.809]; although the exposed Ky/MSI-high cell has only 27 observations, the lower bound remains enormous, so I accept it as a dataset-specific context association while noting small-cell caution. For KEAP1-loss versus weaker NFE2L2 dependency within Ky, R29 is +0.787 [0.741, 0.832]. The adherent-culture direct tests are similarly strong: WRN/MSI-high +0.816 [0.784, 0.849], SMARCA2/SMARCA4-loss +0.786 [0.762, 0.810], and NFE2L2/KEAP1-loss +0.795 [0.770, 0.820]. I accept H36-H41 as dataset-specific within-context associations supporting the robustness of the accepted trio, not as independent validation.\n\nThe most important new mechanistic result is TP53 loss versus dependency_USP7. With direction +1, a positive signed estimate means TP53-loss cells have less negative USP7 dependency scores, i.e., weaker USP7 dependency. R38 is +0.804 [0.783, 0.825], an extremely large and precise dataset-specific association. It is mechanistically plausible because USP7 functions in p53/MDM2-related regulation, and TP53 loss could reduce reliance on USP7; however, this remains only an association in the supplied data. I accept H48 and keep it active, with context follow-up proposed before deciding whether it should become a leading validated claim.\n\nThe other new mechanistic tests are mostly null or imprecise. KRAS mutation versus dependency_RIT1, R33, is +0.003 with interval [-0.016, 0.023]; the upper bound is below the approximate 10% RIT1 score-scale benchmark, so I reject H42. BRAF V600E versus RIT1, R34, and ERBB2 amplification versus RIT1, R35, are near zero but have wide intervals that touch borderline clinically meaningful values in their claimed directions; H43 and H44 remain unresolved but deferred because the point estimates are negligible and the RIT1 panel otherwise gives little support. MYC amplification versus DHX9, R36, is near null with a borderline negative lower bound, so H46 is unresolved but deferred. TP53 loss versus RPL11, R37, is also near null with a borderline positive upper bound, so H47 is unresolved but deferred.\n\nI request independent validation for H12. The central SMARCA4-loss/dependency_SMARCA2 association is large in the full eligible sample and now shows very large direct effects in adenocarcinoma, Ky, and adherent contexts; external validation would distinguish robust replication from shared same-dataset structure or correlated genomic confounding. H48 is the next validation candidate after its context tests, and H13 would remain a later candidate. All conclusions remain associations in this dataset; unadjusted Welch comparisons can be confounded by correlated alterations, multiple testing is present, and no causal or broadly generalizable claim is made.","synthesize":"The new validation decisively strengthens H12 and disposes of the unresolved H4. For H12, SMARCA4-loss versus dependency_SMARCA2, discovery R12 was +0.782 [0.761, 0.802], signed to the hypothesis that SMARCA4-loss cells have stronger, more negative SMARCA2 dependency. Independent validation R39 was +0.805 [0.775, 0.836] under the stricter validation-adjusted interval. The lower bounds are far above any reasonable approximate 10% effect benchmark on the SMARCA2 score scale, and discovery and validation magnitudes are highly consistent. Therefore H12 is accepted as an independently replicated dataset-specific association, not as a causal or clinical claim. The previously accepted within-context confirmations H26 adenocarcinoma, H36 Ky library, and H40 adherent culture are now treated as completed robustness checks and closed. The borderline Ky interaction H29 also is closed as an investigation line because the central effect is validated and very large in Ky itself, although the interaction estimate remains statistically imprecise and unresolved in a strict sense.\n\nFor H4, EGFR amplification versus dependency_EGFR, the response-deadline validation is negative for the registered hypothesis. record.narrative: I am using this analysis block primarily to determine whether the large TP53-loss/weaker-USP7 association (H48/R38) is robust enough to become the next independent-validation target and whether it could be confounded or modified by MTAP-loss co-deletion. I also request direct MTAP-loss effects on USP7 and MDM2 (H58 and H59) because MTAP deletion is biologically and genomically plausible as a confounder or modifier of p53-pathway dependency relationships. If H48 remains large across contexts and MTAP direct effects do not dominate, I will likely request independent validation of H48 in appraisal. The remaining six analyses provide scientifically informative breadth and specificity checks: H66 tests whether the accepted SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 association persists within ARID1A-loss cells; H55 and H56 begin broad coverage of untested KIF18A dependency under MYC amplification and TP53 loss; and H65 and H67 test whether TP53 loss has broader p53-associated effects on transcription-stress/helicase nodes POLR2A and DHX9, helping distinguish a selective USP7 effect from a general p53-loss signature. I also registered downstream RAS/MAPK cross-dependency tests: KRAS or BRAF alterations may reduce dependence on upstream EGFR or KRAS itself, and KRAS mutation may reduce dependence on ERBB2. Finally, I registered TP53-loss versus POLR2A and DHX9 to ask whether p53 loss changes transcription-stress or helicase/R-loop dependencies, and a SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 context test within ARID1A-loss cells because ARID1A loss may modify chromatin-remodeler dependencies even though the direct ARID1A effect was null. I also request direct MTAP-loss effects on USP7 and MDM2 (H58 and H59) because MTAP deletion is biologically and genomically plausible as a confounder or modifier of p53-pathway dependency relationships. For SMARCA4-loss versus dependency_SMARCA2 within the Ky library, R27 is signed to the negative-dependency hypothesis and is +0.814 with a 95% interval [0.774, 0.855]. This is far above a conservative ~10% score-scale benchmark and resolves the earlier borderline Ky interaction by showing that the main SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 effect remains very large inside Ky cells. For MSI-high versus dependency_WRN within Ky, R28 is +0.751 [0.693, 0.809]; although the exposed Ky/MSI-high cell has only 27 observations, the lower bound remains enormous, so I accept it as a dataset-specific context association while noting small-cell caution. For KEAP1-loss versus weaker NFE2L2 dependency within Ky, R29 is +0.787 [0.741, 0.832]. The adherent-culture direct tests are similarly strong: WRN/MSI-high +0.816 [0.784, 0.849], SMARCA2/SMARCA4-loss +0.786 [0.762, 0.810], and NFE2L2/KEAP1-loss +0.795 [0.770, 0.820]. I accept H36-H41 as dataset-specific within-context associations supporting the robustness of the accepted trio, not as independent validation.\n\nThe most important new mechanistic result is TP53 loss versus dependency_USP7. With direction +1, a positive signed estimate means TP53-loss cells have less negative USP7 dependency scores, i.e., weaker USP7 dependency. R38 is +0.804 [0.783, 0.825], an extremely large and precise dataset-specific association. It is mechanistically plausible because USP7 functions in p53/MDM2-related regulation, and TP53 loss could reduce reliance on USP7; however, this remains only an association in the supplied data. I accept H48 and keep it active, with context follow-up proposed before deciding whether it should become a leading validated claim.\n\nThe other new mechanistic tests are mostly null or imprecise. KRAS mutation versus dependency_RIT1, R33, is +0.003 with interval [-0.016, 0.023]; the upper bound is below the approximate 10% RIT1 score-scale benchmark, so I reject H42. BRAF V600E versus RIT1, R34, and ERBB2 amplification versus RIT1, R35, are near zero but have wide intervals that touch borderline clinically meaningful values in their claimed directions; H43 and H44 remain unresolved but deferred because the point estimates are negligible and the RIT1 panel otherwise gives little support. record.narrative:
The new TP53-loss/USP7 context tests strongly support the central accepted association and justify independent validation of the full-sample claim H48. The signed direction is +1 for TP53 loss versus weaker USP7 dependency, and all four direct context effects are large and precise: adenocarcinoma R40 is +0.803 [0.778, 0.827], Ky library R41 is +0.769 [0.727, 0.812], adherent culture R42 is +0.803 [0.779, 0.827], and MTAP-loss cells R44 is +0.758 [0.709, 0.808]. These are far above any conservative approximate 10% effect benchmark on the dependency-score scale, and the MTAP-loss subgroup lower bound remains very large despite only 69 exposed observations. I therefore accept H51, H52, H53, and H57 as dataset-specific context support and close them as completed robustness checks for H48.

The MTAP-loss interaction H54 is a useful confounding check but does not support the registered positive interaction. R43 is negative, -0.056 [-0.111, -0.002], indicating a small attenuation of the TP53-loss/weaker-USP7 association in MTAP-loss cells rather than enhancement. Because the main effect remains large within MTAP-loss cells and the interaction magnitude is small relative to the main ~0.76-0.80 effects, I reject H54 as an enhanced MTAP-loss modification claim and close it. Direct MTAP-loss effects on USP7 and MDM2, R45 and R46, are near null and imprecise; H58 and H59 remain unresolved but deferred. They do not show that MTAP loss alone is a dominant driver strong enough to invalidate H48, though correlated 9p co-deletion remains a caution when interpreting this association.

H66 adds a second robustness check for the already independently validated SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 association: within ARID1A-loss cells, SMARCA4 loss remains associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency, R47 is +0.805 [0.755, 0.854]. I accept H66 and close it as a completed context check; it does not require separate validation because H12 is already validated.

The p53-specificity checks are informative. H65 is null/near-null for TP53 loss versus weaker POLR2A dependency: R50 is -0.014 [-0.035, 0.007], and the upper bound is well below a rough clinical benchmark, so I reject the positive POLR2A hypothesis. H67 also does not support the registered stronger DHX9 direction; R51 is negative, -0.024 [-0.044, -0.004], indicating a small opposite direction rather than the claimed association. I reject H67 for the registered hypothesis. Together, these results make the TP53-loss/USP7 association look more selective than a broad p53-loss effect on transcription or helicase dependencies, although residual specificity uncertainty remains.

The KIF18A tests remain near-null but are not fully conclusive for small clinically meaningful effects: H55 MYC amplification R48 is +0.009 [-0.015, 0.032], and H56 TP53 loss R49 is +0.019 [-0.002, 0.041]. I leave H55 and H56 unresolved and deferred because point estimates are small, intervals include zero, and the upper tails may touch a borderline benchmark; these are low priority relative to H48 validation. Overall, the evidence now supports requesting independent validation for H48. This would test whether the large TP53-loss/weaker-USP7 association is robust beyond the discovery partition and correlated same-dataset structure. All conclusions remain dataset-specific associations, not causal claims or generalized clinical claims.

Maintain that all accepted claims are associations in this supplied dataset/validation split, not causal or generalizable clinical findings.","latest_stage_narratives":{"explore":"The next highest-value exploration is to resolve whether the very large TP53-loss/weaker-USP7 association is robust and whether it is confounded or modified by MTAP loss, a common co-deleted 9p alteration near CDKN2A/p53-related biology. If the USP7 association is stable across TP53-loss contexts and is not merely tracking MTAP co-loss, H48 should become the next independent validation target. I also registered downstream RAS/MAPK cross-dependency tests: KRAS or BRAF alterations may reduce dependence on upstream EGFR or KRAS itself, and KRAS mutation may reduce dependence on ERBB2. These are distinct from the earlier rejected EGFR-amplification results and test pathway position rather than receptor amplification. ERBB2 amplification versus STAT3 and TMED10 tests receptor-driven signaling dependencies beyond EGFR amplification. Finally, I registered TP53-loss versus POLR2A and DHX9 to ask whether p53 loss changes transcription-stress or helicase/R-loop dependencies, and a SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 context test within ARID1A-loss cells because ARID1A loss may modify chromatin-remodeler dependencies even though the direct ARID1A effect was null. These proposals preserve the current validation plan: first confirm H48 contexts, then request independent validation for H48 if consistent; H13 remains the next major unvalidated candidate after that.","analyze":"I am using this analysis block primarily to determine whether the large TP53-loss/weaker-USP7 association (H48/R38) is robust enough to become the next independent-validation target and whether it could be confounded or modified by MTAP-loss co-deletion. I also request direct MTAP-loss effects on USP7 and MDM2 (H58 and H59) because MTAP deletion is biologically and genomically plausible as a confounder or modifier of p53-pathway dependency relationships. If H48 remains large across contexts and MTAP direct effects do not dominate, I will likely request independent validation of H48 in appraisal. The remaining six analyses provide scientifically informative breadth and specificity checks: H66 tests whether the accepted SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 association persists within ARID1A-loss cells; H55 and H56 begin broad coverage of untested KIF18A dependency under MYC amplification and TP53 loss; and H65 and H67 test whether TP53 loss has broader p53-associated effects on transcription-stress/helicase nodes POLR2A and DHX9, helping distinguish a selective USP7 effect from a general p53-loss signature. I defer the newly registered EGFR/KRAS downstream tests and TMED10/ERBB2 tests for now because the EGFR-dependency line has already failed validation and the TMED10/ERBB2 hypothesis is more speculative.","appraise":"The new TP53-loss/USP7 context tests strongly support the central accepted association and justify independent validation of the full-sample claim H48. The signed direction is +1 for TP53 loss versus weaker USP7 dependency, and all four direct context effects are large and precise: adenocarcinoma R40 is +0.803 [0.778, 0.827], Ky library R41 is +0.769 [0.727, 0.812], adherent culture R42 is +0.803 [0.779, 0.827], and MTAP-loss cells R44 is +0.758 [0.709, 0.808]. These are far above any conservative approximate 10% effect benchmark on the dependency-score scale, and the MTAP-loss subgroup lower bound remains very large despite only 69 exposed observations. I therefore accept H51, H52, H53, and H57 as dataset-specific context support and close them as completed robustness checks for H48.\n\nThe MTAP-loss interaction H54 is a useful confounding check but does not support the registered positive interaction. R43 is negative, -0.056 [-0.111, -0.002], indicating a small attenuation of the TP53-loss/weaker-USP7 association in MTAP-loss cells rather than enhancement. Because the main effect remains large within MTAP-loss cells and the interaction magnitude is small relative to the main ~0.76-0.80 effects, I reject H54 as an enhanced MTAP-loss modification claim and close it. Direct MTAP-loss effects on USP7 and MDM2, R45 and R46, are near null and imprecise; H58 and H59 remain unresolved but deferred. They do not show that MTAP loss alone is a dominant driver strong enough to invalidate H48, though correlated 9p co-deletion remains a caution when interpreting this association.\n\nH66 adds a second robustness check for the already independently validated SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 association: within ARID1A-loss cells, SMARCA4 loss remains associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency, R47 is +0.805 [0.755, 0.854]. I accept H66 and close it as a completed context check; it does not require separate validation because H12 is already validated.\n\nThe p53-specificity checks are informative. H65 is null/near-null for TP53 loss versus weaker POLR2A dependency: R50 is -0.014 [-0.035, 0.007], and the upper bound is well below a rough clinical benchmark, so I reject the positive POLR2A hypothesis. H67 also does not support the registered stronger DHX9 direction; R51 is negative, -0.024 [-0.044, -0.004], indicating a small opposite direction rather than the claimed association. I reject H67 for the registered hypothesis. record.narrative:
The delivered validation resolves both pending deadlines. For H11, MSI-high versus dependency_WRN, the independent validation R26 is +0.797 with lower bound 0.744, while discovery R11 was +0.790 with lower bound 0.760. The direction, magnitude, and practical significance are highly consistent, and both lower bounds are far above any conservative approximate 10% dependency-score benchmark. I therefore keep H11 accepted and close it as an independently replicated dataset-specific association: MSI-high cells show much stronger WRN dependency in this supplied dataset. For H48, TP53 loss versus weaker USP7 dependency, validation R52 is +0.7995 with lower bound 0.768, closely matching discovery R38 +0.804 [0.783,0.825] and the large direct context effects in adenocarcinoma, Ky library, adherent culture, and MTAP-loss cells. I accept H48 and close its investigation as robust within the supplied discovery/validation structure. This is not causal evidence, but it is now one of the strongest supported associations: TP53-loss cells have weaker USP7 dependency. The MTAP-loss checks do not invalidate it: direct MTAP effects were near null, and the MTAP-loss interaction was a small attenuation, not an enhancement, of the TP53 loss effect. The p53 specificity checks also make the USP7 association look relatively selective: TP53 loss was not meaningfully associated with the registered POLR2A hypothesis and did not support the registered stronger DHX9 hypothesis. 

The independently replicated core now includes H11, H12, and H48. The largest remaining unvalidated accepted effect is H13, KEAP1 loss versus weaker NFE2L2 dependency. It is supported by a very large discovery estimate and multiple context-specific confirmations, but it still needs independent validation. I therefore reopened H13 as active and closed the context-specific NFE2L2 confirmations as completed robustness checks. Next analyses should prioritize independent validation of H13, while also running the registered marker modifier tests H17-H23. The new proposals add biologically motivated follow-up: whether STK11 loss modifies the KEAP1/NFE2L2 or MSI/WRN associations, whether ARID1A loss modifies the SMARCA4/SMARCA2 interaction, whether BRCA2 loss increases DHX9 or POLR2A dependency, and whether CDKN2A loss or PTEN loss produce p53- or USP7-related dependency shifts that might indicate broader pathway co-occurrence effects. Negative findings remain important: EGFR amplification failed independent validation for EGFR dependency; KRAS/BRAF/RIT1/ERBB2 contrasts were mostly near null; several MTAP and marker interactions are unresolved but low priority; and constructed markers D/E/F still lack clear interpretation beyond assay controls. All accepted claims remain dataset-specific associations, not causal effects or guaranteed generalizable clinical claims.

record.narrative:
The current strongest validated dataset-specific effects are MSI-high versus stronger WRN dependency, SMARCA4-loss versus stronger SMARCA2 dependency, and TP53-loss versus weaker USP7 dependency. The next highest-priority scientific target is independent validation of KEAP1-loss versus weaker NFE2L2 dependency, but at the explore stage I am registering additional falsifiable comparisons that either broaden pathway coverage or provide specificity/confounding checks around the accepted and near-accepted effects.

First, I registered PIK3CA-mutation effects on STAT3, EGFR, and ERBB2. PIK3CA activating mutations constitutively activate downstream PI3K/AKT signaling. This could increase STAT3 dependency through kinase-signaling crosstalk, so I proposed PIK3CA versus stronger STAT3 dependency under direction -1. If downstream PI3K activation bypasses upstream receptor input, PIK3CA-mutant cells could have weaker dependency on EGFR or ERBB2; I therefore proposed positive mean differences for EGFR and ERBB2, meaning less negative dependency scores and therefore weaker dependency. The alternative is null because STAT3 may be largely independent of PIK3CA, or because receptor-dependency relationships are lineage and mutation-context dependent.

Second, I registered NF1-loss effects on STAT3 and KRAS. NF1 is a RAS-GTPase-activating protein, so NF1 loss should produce elevated RAS-MAPK activity. A plausible hypothesis is that NF1-loss tumors are more dependent on STAT3, a stress-signaling node downstream of inflammatory and growth-factor pathways, so the registered STAT3 claim expects stronger, more negative dependency. For KRAS, NF1 loss could increase addiction to KRAS-GTP signaling, but it could also make KRAS less selectively required because other RAS isoforms or downstream effectors compensate; I still registered stronger KRAS dependency as a falsifiable hypothesis but will treat any negative or small estimate as informative against the simple NF1-loss-to-KRAS-dependence model.

Third, I registered a receptor-crosstalk comparison: ERBB2 amplification versus EGFR dependency. EGFR and ERBB2 form heterodimers and share downstream signaling. ERBB2 amplification could compensate for EGFR, producing weaker EGFR dependency, which is the positive raw exposed-minus-comparator hypothesis. Alternatively, ERBB2-amplified cells might retain or co-select EGFR pathway dependence, producing a negative raw contrast. This comparison adds a new receptor-dependency relationship rather than repeating the failed EGFR-amplification direct dependency line.

Fourth, I registered BRCA2-loss versus KIF18A dependency. BRCA2 loss creates homologous-recombination deficiency and genome instability. KIF18A is mitotic and often exposed by replication-stress or mitotic checkpoint defects. A stronger, more negative KIF18A dependency would be consistent with BRCA2-deficient cells being more vulnerable to mitotic spindle control loss. The alternative is specificity: BRCA2 may alter DNA repair dependencies such as DHX9 or POLR2A without changing KIF18A.

Fifth, I registered MSI-high versus DHX9 dependency. MSI-high is already associated with a very large WRN-dependency effect in this dataset. Testing MSI-high against DHX9 asks whether MSI broadly increases dependency on DNA/R-loop-associated helicase nodes or whether the MSI association is relatively WRN-selective. The registered direction is stronger DHX9 dependency with MSI-high, but a null result would support WRN specificity and would not invalidate the validated MSI/WRN association.

Sixth, I registered modification checks using CDKN2A loss. CDKN2A co-deletion or pathway alteration is a natural confounding context for the TP53-loss/USP7 association and also biologically relevant to MDM2. The interaction claims test whether the TP53-loss contrast differs in CDKN2A-loss versus non-loss cells. A positive interaction for USP7 would mean the TP53-loss/weaker-USP7 contrast is even larger in CDKN2A-loss cells; a negative interaction would mean attenuation. Direct CDKN2A-loss versus USP7 is also registered because if CDKN2A loss alone is associated with weaker USP7 dependency, the TP53-loss USP7 association may partly reflect broader p53- or cell-cycle-pathway co-alteration rather than a uniquely TP53-loss-specific association. These are context and specificity checks, not reasons to discard H48 unless they reveal a dominant direct or interaction effect.

Finally, I registered a KEAP1-loss-by-MYC-amplification interaction for dependency_NFE2L2. KEAP1 loss is currently accepted as associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, and the interaction asks whether MYC amplification changes that relationship. MYC amplification may increase oxidative and metabolic stress, potentially changing NRF2-pathway dependencies. This is biologically motivated and directly related to the major unvalidated candidate H13, although independent validation of H13 remains the next central priority. All new comparisons are treated as dataset-specific associations; none should be interpreted as causal or generally clinically actionable unless further evidence and independent validation support it.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

record.narrative:
The new evidence mostly provides negative specificity and context checks around the central accepted effects. For the constructed markers, H17/R53, H18/R54, H19/R55, H21/R56, H22/R57, and H23/R58 are all small and imprecise. Their signed estimates are near zero, and the 95% upper bounds are roughly 0.028-0.060, below the approximate 0.1 dependency-score benchmark I am using to distinguish trivial from scientifically meaningful associations. These nulls do not create scientific claims; they instead suggest that the large WRN/SMARCA2/NFE2L2 associations are not tracking arbitrary marker-positive groups. I therefore reject the registered marker main-effect and marker-interaction claims as completed negative controls and close them. 

The culture interaction results are mixed but mostly reassuring. H32/R60 for SMARCA2 and H33/R61 for NFE2L2 are null, with upper bounds 0.0596 and 0.0391, below the practical benchmark; I reject those as meaningful modifiers of the validated SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 and accepted KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 relationships. H31/R59 for MSI-high/WRN is the only borderline culture result: the signed interaction is +0.114 with 95% interval [0.041, 0.187]. The point estimate is above the benchmark, but the lower bound is below it, so I leave H31 unresolved and deferred rather than accepting a clinically meaningful culture modification. Importantly, this borderline interaction does not invalidate the independently validated H11 MSI-high/WRN association, because the adherent-culture main effect remains extremely large at R30 = +0.816 [0.784, 0.849]. 

The STK11 checks also support specificity of the KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 relationship. H69/R62 tests whether STK11 loss modifies the KEAP1-loss contrast; the signed estimate is -0.029 [-0.088, 0.030], so the upper bound is well below the benchmark and the registered direction is unsupported. H70/R63 tests STK11 loss alone against NFE2L2 dependency; the signed estimate is -0.023 [-0.065, 0.018], again null. I reject H69 and H70 as completed checks and close them. The MSI-high/STK11 interaction H71/R64 is uninformative because the MSI-high and STK11-loss interaction cell has only 19 observations and the Welch analysis is invalid. I leave H71 unresolved but close it because this exact stratification is underpowered and future effort should go to independent validation of H13. 

I am requesting independent validation for H13, KEAP1 loss versus weaker NFE2L2 dependency. This is the largest accepted but unvalidated effect. The main discovery association is R7 = +0.797 [0.776, 0.819], and it is supported by context effects in adenocarcinoma R16 = +0.795, Ky library R29 = +0.787, and adherent culture R32 = +0.795. The new robustness checks reduce concern that the KEAP1/NFE2L2 association is explained by marker-D assay artifacts, culture environment, or STK11 co-alteration: marker D direct and interaction effects are null, culture interaction is null, and STK11 direct and interaction effects are null. This does not establish causality or clinical generalizability, but it makes H13 the best next candidate for independent validation. All accepted associations remain dataset-specific statistical associations. 

From a critical-reviewer perspective, the main threats are multiplicity and correlated genomic co-alterations. I am not accepting the borderline H31 culture interaction because its interval includes clinically trivial effects, and I am treating marker D/E/F tests as arbitrary-assay controls rather than biological pathways. The central validated claims H11, H12, and H48 remain distinct from the exploratory negative controls.

The next highest-priority scientific target is independent validation of KEAP1-loss versus weaker NFE2L2 dependency, but at the explore stage I am registering additional falsifiable comparisons that either broaden pathway coverage or provide specificity/confounding checks around the accepted and near-accepted effects.\n\nFirst, I registered PIK3CA-mutation effects on STAT3, EGFR, and ERBB2. PIK3CA activating mutations constitutively activate downstream PI3K/AKT signaling. This could increase STAT3 dependency through kinase-signaling crosstalk, so I proposed PIK3CA versus stronger STAT3 dependency under direction -1. If downstream PI3K activation bypasses upstream receptor input, PIK3CA-mutant cells could have weaker dependency on EGFR or ERBB2; I therefore proposed positive mean differences for EGFR and ERBB2, meaning less negative dependency scores and therefore weaker dependency. The alternative is null because STAT3 may be largely independent of PIK3CA, or because receptor-dependency relationships are lineage and mutation-context dependent.\n\nSecond, I registered NF1-loss effects on STAT3 and KRAS. NF1 is a RAS-GTPase-activating protein, so NF1 loss should produce elevated RAS-MAPK activity. A plausible hypothesis is that NF1-loss tumors are more dependent on STAT3, a stress-signaling node downstream of inflammatory and growth-factor pathways, so the registered STAT3 claim expects stronger, more negative dependency. For KRAS, NF1 loss could increase addiction to KRAS-GTP signaling, but it could also make KRAS less selectively required because other RAS isoforms or downstream effectors compensate; I still registered stronger KRAS dependency as a falsifiable hypothesis but will treat any negative or small estimate as informative against the simple NF1-loss-to-KRAS-dependence model.\n\nThird, I registered a receptor-crosstalk comparison: ERBB2 amplification versus EGFR dependency. EGFR and ERBB2 form heterodimers and share downstream signaling. ERBB2 amplification could compensate for EGFR, producing weaker EGFR dependency, which is the positive raw exposed-minus-comparator hypothesis. Alternatively, ERBB2-amplified cells might retain or co-select EGFR pathway dependence, producing a negative raw contrast. This comparison adds a new receptor-dependency relationship rather than repeating the failed EGFR-amplification direct dependency line.\n\nFourth, I registered BRCA2-loss versus KIF18A dependency. BRCA2 loss creates homologous-recombination deficiency and genome instability. KIF18A is mitotic and often exposed by replication-stress or mitotic checkpoint defects. A stronger, more negative KIF18A dependency would be consistent with BRCA2-deficient cells being more vulnerable to mitotic spindle control loss. The alternative is specificity: BRCA2 may alter DNA repair dependencies such as DHX9 or POLR2A without changing KIF18A.\n\nFifth, I registered MSI-high versus DHX9 dependency. record.narrative:
The delivered validation resolves the two due claims and completes the main independent-validation stage for the strongest associations. For H12, the independent validation R39 is signed +0.805 [0.775, 0.836] for the hypothesis that SMARCA4-loss cells have stronger SMARCA2 dependency, closely matching discovery R12 at +0.782 [0.761, 0.802]. Because the lower bound is far above any reasonable 10-percent practical benchmark and the direction and magnitude are replicated, I keep H12 accepted and close it as a dataset-specific association: SMARCA4-loss cells have stronger SMARCA2 dependency in this supplied dataset. For H13, the independent validation R65 is signed +0.804 [0.773, 0.835] for the refined hypothesis that KEAP1-loss cells have weaker NFE2L2 dependency, closely matching discovery R7 at +0.797 [0.776, 0.819]. This is very large and precisely estimated, so I accept and close H13. The signed direction means the raw KEAP1-loss minus KEAP1-non-loss difference is positive, i.e. less negative NFE2L2 scores and therefore weaker dependency. The opposite claim H7 is now explicitly rejected because the same validation strongly contradicts stronger NFE2L2 dependency in KEAP1-loss cells.

The supported core now consists of four independently replicated dataset-specific associations: MSI-high versus stronger WRN dependency (H11), SMARCA4-loss versus stronger SMARCA2 dependency (H12), TP53-loss versus weaker USP7 dependency (H48), and KEAP1-loss versus weaker NFE2L2 dependency (H13). Each has discovery and validation estimates near 0.8 with lower bounds well above the practical benchmark. Context-specific confirmations and null modifier checks reduce concern that these are simple artifacts of lineage, CRISPR library, culture, constructed marker assays, or tested co-alterations. For H13, adenocarcinoma, Ky-library, and adherent-culture direct effects are large and positive, whereas marker D, culture-interaction, and STK11 direct/interaction tests are null. For H48, context effects in adenocarcinoma, Ky-library, adherent culture, and MTAP-loss cells remain large; direct MTAP effects and MTAP-by-TP53 interaction do not support a dominant co-deletion explanation, although correlated 9p biology remains a caution.

Negative and low-priority findings are scientifically useful. EGFR amplification did not replicate as a clinically meaningful dependency association in EGFR dependency (H4 failed validation). KRAS-mutation contrasts for KRAS, BRAF, EGFR, ERBB2, and RIT1 dependencies are mostly near null or imprecise. Many small effects involving MYC amplification, TP53 loss, MTAP loss, p53-pathway co-alterations, KIF18A, POLR2A, RPL11, DHX9, and receptor pathway markers remain below the practical benchmark or unresolved and should not be accepted. Constructed markers D/E/F behaved as null controls and should not be interpreted as biological pathways. The STK11 checks for NFE2L2 and KEAP1 were null; the MSI-high STK11 interaction was underpowered. The only borderline context modifier is H31, where the adherent-culture interaction for MSI-high versus WRN dependency is +0.114 [0.041, 0.187]. Its point estimate crosses the practical benchmark, but its lower bound does not, so it remains unresolved and does not overturn H11, whose main and adherent-culture effects remain enormous.

Unresolved uncertainty is mainly residual confounding by correlated genomic alterations, underpowered subgroup interactions, and lack of causal or external-generalizability evidence. These results establish associations in the supplied dataset/validation structure, not mechanisms of dependency, not necessarily causal driver relationships, and not guaranteed clinical biomarker claims.

The most informative next analysis is to test specificity and modifiers of the validated core rather than pursue near-null small main effects. I prioritize the already active CDKN2A checks around p53 biology (H85/H86/H88), BRCA2/MSI DNA-repair selectivity tests (H73/H74/H83/H84), MYC amplification modification of the KEAP1-loss effect (H87), and receptor/PI3K/NF1 crosstalk tests (H77-H82). I also register two negative-control comparisons: KEAP1 loss versus WRN dependency and KEAP1 loss versus SMARCA2 dependency. These are expected to be null if the KEAP1 association is NFE2L2-selective; a large effect would indicate a broader dependency pattern and would require reevaluation of specificity.

The next highest-priority scientific target is independent validation of KEAP1-loss versus weaker NFE2L2 dependency, but at the explore stage I am registering additional falsifiable comparisons that either broaden pathway coverage or provide specificity/confounding checks around the accepted and near-accepted effects.\n\nFirst, I registered PIK3CA-mutation effects on STAT3, EGFR, and ERBB2. PIK3CA activating mutations constitutively activate downstream PI3K/AKT signaling. This could increase STAT3 dependency through kinase-signaling crosstalk, so I proposed PIK3CA versus stronger STAT3 dependency under direction -1. If downstream PI3K activation bypasses upstream receptor input, PIK3CA-mutant cells could have weaker dependency on EGFR or ERBB2; I therefore proposed positive mean differences for EGFR and ERBB2, meaning less negative dependency scores and therefore weaker dependency. The alternative is null because STAT3 may be largely independent of PIK3CA, or because receptor-dependency relationships are lineage and mutation-context dependent.\n\nSecond, I registered NF1-loss effects on STAT3 and KRAS. NF1 is a RAS-GTPase-activating protein, so NF1 loss should produce elevated RAS-MAPK activity. A plausible hypothesis is that NF1-loss tumors are more dependent on STAT3, a stress-signaling node downstream of inflammatory and growth-factor pathways, so the registered STAT3 claim expects stronger, more negative dependency. For KRAS, NF1 loss could increase addiction to KRAS-GTP signaling, but it could also make KRAS less selectively required because other RAS isoforms or downstream effectors compensate; I still registered stronger KRAS dependency as a falsifiable hypothesis but will treat any negative or small estimate as informative against the simple NF1-loss-to-KRAS-dependence model.\n\nThird, I registered a receptor-crosstalk comparison: ERBB2 amplification versus EGFR dependency. EGFR and ERBB2 form heterodimers and share downstream signaling. ERBB2 amplification could compensate for EGFR, producing weaker EGFR dependency, which is the positive raw exposed-minus-comparator hypothesis. Alternatively, ERBB2-amplified cells might retain or co-select EGFR pathway dependence, producing a negative raw contrast. This comparison adds a new receptor-dependency relationship rather than repeating the failed EGFR-amplification direct dependency line.\n\nFourth, I registered BRCA2-loss versus KIF18A dependency. BRCA2 loss creates homologous-recombination deficiency and genome instability. KIF18A is mitotic and often exposed by replication-stress or mitotic checkpoint defects. A stronger, more negative KIF18A dependency would be consistent with BRCA2-deficient cells being more vulnerable to mitotic spindle control loss. The alternative is specificity: BRCA2 may alter DNA repair dependencies such as DHX9 or POLR2A without changing KIF18A.\n\nFifth, I registered MSI-high versus DHX9 dependency. record.narrative:
There are no assessments_due at this explore stage, so I am not changing existing scientific conclusions. The accepted validated core is MSI-high versus stronger WRN dependency, SMARCA4-loss versus stronger SMARCA2 dependency, TP53-loss versus weaker USP7 dependency, and KEAP1-loss versus weaker NFE2L2 dependency. The next useful comparisons should test whether these large associations are biologically specific, robust to CRISPR-screen quality, and not explained by common co-alterations or pathway bypass contexts.  

I registered co-alteration refinements for the two most important non-MRE pathway dependencies: TP53-loss by SMARCA4-loss for USP7 dependency, and KEAP1-loss by TP53-loss for NFE2L2 dependency. These ask whether the main dependency contrast is enlarged or attenuated in a relevant co-altered tumor-suppressor context. A large attenuation would suggest that correlated losses confound the main association; a large enhancement would define a context where the dependency is especially strong. Because I expect independence more than a strong interaction, the anticipated direction is uncertain, and I will only accept a meaningful interaction if the signed effect is large and the interval remains above the practical dependency benchmark.  

I registered PI3K/RAS/receptor crosstalk checks: PIK3CA mutation effects on EGFR dependency modified by KRAS mutation, and ERBB2 amplification effects on ERBB2 dependency modified by PIK3CA mutation. If downstream PI3K activation bypasses upstream receptor input, receptor-dependency differences should be smaller in PIK3CA-mutant cells, giving a negative interaction. Conversely, if receptor pathway activation remains required, estimates will be near zero or positive. These comparisons broaden beyond the earlier EGFR-amplification line, which failed validation, and test pathway redundancy in a falsifiable way.  

I registered CRISPR-activity robustness interactions using high Cas9 activity, cas9_activity_pct >= 75%, for each core association: MSI-high/WRN, SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2, TP53-loss/USP7, and KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2. Cas9 activity is a measured technical predictor, so a dependency association that depends only on high-Cas9 cells would be more screen-quality driven, whereas an association similar across high and lower Cas9 strata would be more robust. I expect null or small interactions, and these should not replace the central main effects unless they are large and consistently signed.  

Finally, I registered direct STK11-loss versus WRN and SMARCA2 dependencies as specificity controls. STK11 loss was previously null for the KEAP1/NFE2L2 contrast, but direct tests against WRN and SMARCA2 clarify whether STK11 co-alteration is broadly associated with these validated dependencies. I expect null effects; large effects would indicate broader lung cancer context dependence and would require revisiting the specificity of the main effects. All proposals are same-dataset association tests and will be interpreted as dataset-specific associations, not causal mechanisms or guaranteed clinical biomarkers.

record.narrative:
I assess all newly delivered discovery results. All 12 new estimates are small relative to the validated core effects and do not provide evidence of a clinically meaningful association at the approximate 0.1 dependency-score benchmark. The high-Cas9 interaction tests H95-H98 are particularly useful technical checks: H95/R66 is +0.023 [-0.043, 0.090], H96/R67 +0.018 [-0.028, 0.065], H97/R68 -0.002 [-0.049, 0.045], and H98/R69 -0.007 [-0.057, 0.043]. These intervals include zero and are bounded below the practical benchmark, so they do not support the idea that the MSI-high/WRN, SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2, TP53-loss/USP7, or KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 associations exist only in high-Cas9 screens. I reject these interaction claims and close them as completed robustness checks.

The specificity controls also remain null. H89/R70 tests KEAP1 loss against WRN dependency, +0.002 [-0.034, 0.030], and H90/R71 tests KEAP1 loss against SMARCA2 dependency, +0.009 [-0.033, 0.052]. These nulls reduce concern that KEAP1 loss is a broad nonselective modifier of these validated dependencies and are compatible with NFE2L2-selective specificity. H84/R76 tests MSI-high against DHX9 dependency, signed estimate +0.020 [-0.017, 0.056], which is far weaker than the validated MSI-high/WRN association (~0.8) and does not support a broad DNA-repair or nucleic-acid metabolism dependency effect. H87/R77 tests MYC-amplification modification of KEAP1 loss for NFE2L2, -0.006 [-0.072, 0.061], and does not support a MYC-dependent alteration of the KEAP1 association.

The co-alteration checks similarly do not reveal dominant confounding. H85/R72 tests TP53-loss modification by CDKN2A loss for USP7, +0.011 [-0.038, 0.060]; H88/R73 tests CDKN2A loss main effect on USP7, +0.004 [-0.039, 0.048]; H91/R74 tests TP53-loss modification by SMARCA4 loss for USP7, +0.022 [-0.026, 0.071]. None reach the practical threshold, so they do not undermine the TP53-loss/USP7 claim by suggesting that USP7 dependency is primarily explained by correlated CDKN2A or SMARCA4 co-loss. H92/R75 tests KEAP1-loss modification by TP53 loss for NFE2L2, +0.039 [-0.016, 0.095]; the point estimate is positive and near but below 0.1, with lower bound negative, so it is not accepted as a meaningful context effect and is rejected as a completed check.

From a multiplicity and critical-review perspective, these results are reassuring because they are mostly null after many exploratory stratifications, and the four central associations remain the only effects with effects near 0.8 and tight intervals. The new evidence does not justify accepting a new modifier or creating new context-specific claims. Therefore I close all 12 new due claims as rejected. 

The only active scientific uncertainty that could benefit from validation is H31, the MSI-high/WRN interaction with adherent culture. Its discovery estimate is +0.114 [0.041, 0.187], so the point estimate exceeds the practical benchmark but the interval remains compatible with clinically trivial effects. Validating H31 directly tests whether the independently replicated MSI-high/WRN association is meaningfully modified by culture context. I keep H31 unresolved and active, and request independent validation for H31. The new Cas9, KEAP1-specificity, co-alteration, MYC, and DHX9 checks do not themselves warrant validation because their intervals exclude clinically meaningful effects.

These comparisons broaden beyond the earlier EGFR-amplification line, which failed validation, and test pathway redundancy in a falsifiable way.  \n\nI registered CRISPR-activity robustness interactions using high Cas9 activity, cas9_activity_pct >= 75%, for each core association: MSI-high/WRN, SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2, TP53-loss/USP7, and KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2. Cas9 activity is a measured technical predictor, so a dependency association that depends only on high-Cas9 cells would be more screen-quality driven, whereas an association similar across high and lower Cas9 strata would be more robust. I expect null or small interactions, and these should not replace the central main effects unless they are large and consistently signed.  \n\nFinally, I registered direct STK11-loss versus WRN and SMARCA2 dependencies as specificity controls. STK11 loss was previously null for the KEAP1/NFE2L2 contrast, but direct tests against WRN and SMARCA2 clarify whether STK11 co-alteration is broadly associated with these validated dependencies. These interactions are expected to be small if the core effects are not artifacts of CRISPR-screen performance; large signed effects would require narrowing the corresponding main associations to Cas9-quality strata. H89 and H90 are specificity controls: KEAP1 loss should not have a large association with WRN or SMARCA2 if its association is NFE2L2-selective. H85, H88, and H91 test correlated tumor-suppressor alterations around the TP53-loss/USP7 association, including CDKN2A loss and SMARCA4 loss; large direct or interaction effects would suggest that the USP7 association is partly explained by co-altered p53 or chromatin-remodeling biology. H92 tests whether KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 biology differs in TP53-loss cells, a relevant co-alteration pathway. H84 tests whether the MSI-high effect is broad on another DNA/RNA metabolism dependency, DHX9, or relatively WRN-specific. H87 tests whether MYC amplification modifies the KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 association, which could define a stronger or weaker dependency context. I will accept only large, precisely estimated associations, with interval bounds above the practical ~0.1 dependency-score benchmark, and otherwise treat null or borderline findings as context checks that do not overturn the validated core.","appraise":"I assess all newly delivered discovery results. The high-Cas9 interaction tests H95-H98 are particularly useful technical checks: H95/R66 is +0.023 [-0.043, 0.090], H96/R67 +0.018 [-0.028, 0.065], H97/R68 -0.002 [-0.049, 0.045], and H98/R69 -0.007 [-0.057, 0.043]. These intervals include zero and are bounded below the practical benchmark, so they do not support the idea that the MSI-high/WRN, SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2, TP53-loss/USP7, or KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 associations exist only in high-Cas9 screens. I reject these interaction claims and close them as completed robustness checks.\n\nThe specificity controls also remain null. H89/R70 tests KEAP1 loss against WRN dependency, +0.002 [-0.034, 0.030], and H90/R71 tests KEAP1 loss against SMARCA2 dependency, +0.009 [-0.033, 0.052]. These nulls reduce concern that KEAP1 loss is a broad nonselective modifier of these validated dependencies and are compatible with NFE2L2-selective specificity. H84/R76 tests MSI-high against DHX9 dependency, signed estimate +0.020 [-0.017, 0.056], which is far weaker than the validated MSI-high/WRN association (~0.8) and does not support a broad DNA-repair or nucleic-acid metabolism dependency effect. This is very large and precisely estimated, so I accept and close H13. The opposite claim H7 is now explicitly rejected because the same validation strongly contradicts stronger NFE2L2 dependency in KEAP1-loss cells.\n\nThe supported core now consists of four independently replicated dataset-specific associations: MSI-high versus stronger WRN dependency (H11), SMARCA4-loss versus stronger SMARCA2 dependency (H12), TP53-loss versus weaker USP7 dependency (H48), and KEAP1-loss versus weaker NFE2L2 dependency (H13). KRAS-mutation contrasts for KRAS, BRAF, EGFR, ERBB2, and RIT1 dependencies are mostly near null or imprecise. Many small effects involving MYC amplification, TP53 loss, MTAP loss, p53-pathway co-alterations, KIF18A, POLR2A, RPL11, DHX9, and receptor pathway markers remain below the practical benchmark or unresolved and should not be accepted. Constructed markers D/E/F behaved as null controls and should not be interpreted as biological pathways. The STK11 checks for NFE2L2 and KEAP1 were null; the MSI-high STK11 interaction was underpowered. The only borderline context modifier is H31, where the adherent-culture interaction for MSI-high versus WRN dependency is +0.114 [0.041, 0.187]. Its point estimate crosses the practical benchmark, but its lower bound does not, so it remains unresolved and does not overturn H11, whose main and adherent-culture effects remain enormous.\n\nUnresolved uncertainty is mainly residual confounding by correlated genomic alterations, underpowered subgroup interactions, and lack of causal or external-generalizability evidence. These results establish associations in the supplied dataset/validation structure, not mechanisms of dependency, not necessarily causal driver relationships, and not guaranteed clinical biomarker claims.\n\nThe most informative next analysis is to test specificity and modifiers of the validated core rather than pursue near-null small main effects. record.narrative: The delivered validations require explicit reassessment. H48 reached its validation deadline: independent validation R52 is signed +0.799 with lower bound +0.768 and upper bound +0.831, closely matching discovery R38 at +0.804 with lower bound +0.783 and upper bound +0.825. Because the signed hypothesis direction is +1, the raw contrast is positive, meaning TP53-loss cells have less negative USP7 dependency scores and therefore weaker USP7 dependency. I keep H48 accepted and closed. H31 failed validation: discovery R59 suggested an adherent-culture interaction for MSI-high WRN dependency, signed +0.114 with 95 percent interval +0.041 to +0.187; independent validation R78 is only +0.0236 with interval -0.0865 to +0.1338, spanning zero, clinically trivial, and opposite directions. I reject H31 and close it as unsupported context modification, while preserving H11 and H39 main effects. H55 also fails validation: discovery R48 +0.0090 and validation R79 +0.0126 are near zero; I reject it. The independently supported core remains: H11 MSI-high -> stronger WRN dependency; H12 SMARCA4-loss -> stronger SMARCA2 dependency; H48 TP53-loss -> weaker USP7 dependency; H13 KEAP1-loss -> weaker NFE2L2 dependency. Each has discovery and validation estimates near 0.80 with lower bounds far above the practical absolute benchmark and far above any plausible 10 percent threshold in arbitrary dependency units. Subgroup analyses in adenocarcinoma, Ky library, adherent culture, and ARID1A-loss contexts remain large where tested, whereas Cas9-high, library, lineage, culture, marker D/E/F, and most co-alteration interactions are small. I additionally closed a batch of completed negative same-dataset checks because their point estimates are small, intervals include zero, and validation is not warranted: H1 KRAS mutation vs KRAS dependency, H6 ERBB2 amplification vs ERBB2 dependency, H43 and H44 RIT1 pathway checks, H10 H46 and H55 MYC-amplification checks, H56 and H47 TP53-loss checks on KIF18A and RPL11, H58 and H59 MTAP-loss p53 co-alteration checks, H34 ARID1A direct chromatin control, H35 KEAP1-to-USP7 cross-check, and H14 H16 H20 H29 H30 context interactions. These negative findings are useful because they show the core associations are not explained by broad receptor, MYC, MTAP, ARID1A, constructed-marker, or most technical/context effects. Unresolved scientific uncertainty remains for active no-evidence specificity and pathway tests, especially direct STK11-loss on WRN and SMARCA2 H99 and H100, BRCA2-loss on DHX9 POLR2A and KIF18A H73 H74 and H83, PIK3CA NF1 and ERBB2 crosstalk H77 through H82 and H93 and H94, MDM2 co-alteration checks H75 H86 and H50, and ARID1A interaction H72. These results are associations in the supplied dataset and validation splits, not causal driver relationships or externally generalizable clinical biomarkers.
